abstract: A strategic sender collects data with the goal of persuading a receiver to adopt a new action. The receiver assesses the profitability of adopting the action by following a classical statistics approach: she forms an estimate via the similarity-weighted empirical frequencies of outcomes in past cases, sharing some attributes with the problem at hand. The sender has control over the characteristics of the sampled cases and discloses the outcomes of his study truthfully. We characterize the sender's optimal sampling strategy as the outcome of a greedy algorithm. The sender provides more relevant data–consisting of observations sharing relatively more characteristics with the current problem–when the sampling capacity is low, when a large amount of initial public data is available, and when the estimated benefit of adoption according to this public data is low. Competition between senders curbs incentives for biasing the receiver's estimate and leads to more balanced datasets.
abstract_zh: 一位策略性信息发送者收集数据，旨在说服接收者采纳新行动。接收者遵循经典统计学方法评估采纳行动的盈利性：她通过相似性加权的历史案例结果经验频率形成估计，这些案例与当前问题共享部分属性。发送者可控制抽样案例的特征，并如实披露研究结果。我们通过贪心算法刻画了发送者的最优抽样策略：当抽样能力有限、可获取的初始公共数据量较大、或根据公共数据估算的采纳收益较低时，发送者会提供更多相关数据（即与当前问题共享更多特征的观测值）。发送者之间的竞争会抑制其扭曲接收者估计的动机，从而形成更均衡的数据集。
title: Persuasion with Limited Data: A Case-Based Approach
title_zh: 有限数据下的说服：基于案例的方法

abstract: We develop a two-country business-cycle model of the US and the rest of the world with dollar dominance in trade invoicing, in cross-border credit, and in safe assets. The interplay between these elements---dollar trinity---rationalizes salient features of the Global Financial Cycle in the data: When its tide subsides, the dollar appreciates, financial conditions tighten, the world business cycle slows down, and emerging-market central banks face a trade-off between mitigating the recession and dampening price pressures. We find the dollar is no sideshow in this, but central for the transmission of the Global Financial Cycle to the world economy.
abstract_zh: 我们构建了一个包含美国与世界其他地区的两国商业周期模型，其中美元在贸易计价、跨境信贷和安全资产领域占据主导地位。这些要素之间的相互作用——美元三位一体——合理化了数据中全球金融周期的显著特征：当美元潮汐退去时，美元升值，金融状况收紧，全球商业周期放缓，新兴市场央行面临缓解经济衰退与抑制价格压力之间的权衡。我们发现，美元在此过程中并非配角，而是全球金融周期向世界经济传导的核心环节。

title: Dollar Trinity and the Global Financial Cycle
title_zh: 美元三位一体与全球金融周期

abstract: Firm organizations are designed to compress unit costs in general, and wage costs in particular. We build on this intuition to study how minimum wages affect firms' organizations, production costs and, ultimately, productivity. To this end, we construct a general equilibrium model in which firms rely on optimal hierarchies to optimize the use of labor and associated knowledge (training). The introduction of a minimum wage constraint in such an environment alters firms' optimal strategies when knowledge acquisition costs are large relative to management costs. We calibrate this model on French data to quantify the impact of the large increases in the minimum wage (up to 8.5% in real terms) that occurred for some firms between 2003 and 2006. We find that the endogenous contraction and flattening responses of firms' organizations strongly contributes to mitigating the overall loss in output (simulated at about 2%). This is driven by gains in revenue productivity (by about 4%) and wages (6.8%), while the impact on quantity-based productivity indices is not monotonic across firm types. These results are confirmed in the French data, both qualitatively and quantitatively, by regression analyses combining difference-in-differences and instrumental variable strategies. Further simulations show that the relative cost of minimum wage constraints tends to be amplified in economies with more efficient communication technologies, and mitigated in economies with more efficient information or problem-solving technologies. However, this last result does not hold for large technological shocks, which suggests that the current waves of new AI-based technologies, as well as the massive investments in communication technologies during the recent Covid-19 pandemic, are likely to necessitate a thorough re-examination of cost-benefit analyses of labor market institutions and regulations.
abstract_zh: 企业组织设计的核心目标在于压缩单位成本，尤其是工资成本。基于这一直觉，我们研究最低工资如何影响企业组织、生产成本，并最终影响生产率。为此，我们构建了一个一般均衡模型，其中企业通过最优层级结构来优化劳动力使用及其相关知识（培训）的配置。当知识获取成本相对于管理成本较高时，最低工资约束的引入会改变企业的最优策略。我们利用法国数据对该模型进行校准，以量化2003年至2006年间部分企业面临的最低工资大幅上涨（实际涨幅高达8.5%）的影响。研究发现，企业组织的内生性收缩与扁平化调整显著缓解了总产出损失（模拟结果约为2%）。这一调整通过收入生产率提升（约4%）和工资增长（6.8%）实现，但基于数量的生产率指数在不同类型企业间呈现非单调变化。通过结合双重差分法与工具变量策略的回归分析，这些结果在法国数据中得到了定性与定量层面的验证。进一步模拟表明，在通信技术更高效的经济体中，最低工资约束的相对成本会被放大；而在信息或问题解决技术更高效的经济体中，该成本则被缓解。然而，这一结论在面临重大技术冲击时不再成立，这意味着当前基于人工智能的新技术浪潮，以及近期新冠疫情期间对通信技术的大规模投资，可能需要对劳动力市场制度与监管的成本效益分析进行彻底重新审视。
title: The Minimum Wage in Firms’ Organizations: Productivity Implications
title_zh: 企业组织中的最低工资：生产率影响

abstract: This paper presents new empirical evidence on the behavior of the U.S Treasury market in response to Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announcements during the Global Financial Crisis and the Covid-19 pandemic. We differentiate between announcements related to policy rate changes and those related to lender-of-last-resort liquidity facilities to examine their distinct impacts on the market. High-frequency data on interest rate futures are used to extract the surprise component of FOMC announcements. To also make use of announcements taking place outside the future exchanges trading hours, we show that high-frequency changes in exchange rates can be used to impute commonly used monetary policy surprises. Our findings reveal that policy rate and liquidity announcements decrease Treasury yields substantially but differ in their transmission mechanism. While announcements related to interest rates primarily affect bond yields through expected lower short rates, lender-of-last-resort announcements decrease bond yields by reducing term premia, demonstrating the complementary role of these different policies in stabilizing the Treasury market by influencing intermediaries and interest rates.
abstract_zh: 本文提供了关于全球金融危机和新冠疫情期间美国国债市场对联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC）公告反应的新实证证据。我们区分了与政策利率变动相关的公告和与最后贷款人流动性便利相关的公告，以考察它们对市场的不同影响。利用利率期货的高频数据提取FOMC公告中的意外成分。为充分利用期货交易所交易时间之外的公告，我们证明汇率的高频变化可用于推算常用的货币政策意外。研究结果表明，政策利率和流动性公告显著降低了国债收益率，但其传导机制存在差异。与利率相关的公告主要通过预期短期利率下降影响债券收益率，而最后贷款人公告则通过降低期限溢价来减少债券收益率，这揭示了这些不同政策在通过影响中介机构和利率来稳定国债市场方面的互补作用。
title: The Impact of Monetary Policy and Lender-of-Last-Resort Announcements on the Treasury Market
title_zh: 货币政策与最后贷款人公告对国债市场的影响
